To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fundamental right of third parties and future tenants of the building being constructed to a healthy and harmonious environment is being violated during territorial planning, which is a direct result of violation of territorial planning procedure.

the right to healthy and harmonious residential and work environment is a fundamental human right, which can be infringed by territorial planning, and that third parties are the persons authorised to contest such violations.

the fundamental rights to healthy and harmonious environment are violated by territorial planning decisions, the persons who are authorised to contest such violations are the tenants of neighbouring houses and the future tenants of the houses being constructed, and such violations can be contested in court.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of fundamental right violations in the process of construction of a new house in a fully urbanised territory, as well as the possibility of contesting such violations by third parties.
the problem of environmental protection during urban development and the role of the state in solving it.
the legal regulation of the right to a healthy and harmonious environment and the ways to protect it from violations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fundamental rights of third parties and future tenants of a house under construction are violated if the construction is not approved by the local executive body, if the construction is approved but not carried out in accordance with the approved design and/or if the local executive body does not take measures to prevent or terminate violations of fundamental rights of third party and future tenants of the construction.
the fundamental rights of third parties to a healthy and harmonious environment are not protected in the course of territorial planning.
the fundamental right violations during urban development are not only a problem of the future tenants of the newly constructed building, but also a problem of the third parties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in order to protect the rights of third parties, it is necessary to establish the right of persons authorised to contest violations of the Law on Administrative Procedure to appeal the decisions on construction permits.
the authorisation of the persons authorised to contest violations of environmental law is insufficient and needs to be improved.
the right of third parties to a healthy and harmonious residential and work environment is not sufficiently protected in the current law.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the right of citizens to live in a healthy and harmonious environment is violated by the territorial planning authorities when they fail to take into account the interests of third parties and future tenants of the building being constructed, and when they fail to ensure compliance with environmental standards and requirements.

the Law on Administrative Procedures is not applicable to the case of violation of the right to healthy and harmonious residential and work environment during construction, which is a fundamental right.
the Law on Administrative Procedures does not grant any person the right to contest environmental violations, and the only way to contest such violations is by lodging an appeal with the court.
